content: Action Medical Research is a British charity dedicated to medical research. It was established in 1952 and is headquartered in Horsham, West Sussex. The organization is registered under Charity No. 208701. Prince Philip, Duke of Edinburgh, serves as its patron, while Charles Guthrie, Baron Guthrie of Craigiebank, holds the position of president. Since 1976, Paddington Bear has been the charity's official mascot. The charity was originally founded by Duncan Guthrie under the name National Fund for Poliomyelitis Research. Its primary goal at the time was to eradicate polio, a disease that caused frequent epidemics of paralysis in the UK during the 1940s and 1950s. The organization played a significant role in funding the development of the first British polio vaccine. Following the successful reduction of paralytic polio cases due to the vaccine, the charity expanded its focus. In 1960, it was renamed The National Fund for Research into Poliomyelitis and Other Crippling Diseases, and in 1967, it became The National Fund for Research into Crippling Diseases. Informally, it was known as Action Research for the Crippled Child. In 1990, the name was shortened to Action Research, and in 2003, it adopted its current name, Action Medical Research. Notably, the World Health Organization declared Europe polio-free in 2002, coinciding with the charity's 50th anniversary. The charity has been involved in numerous groundbreaking medical projects, particularly focusing on pregnancy and neonatal health. It has contributed to the development of the rubella vaccine, ultrasound scanning during pregnancy, intrauterine blood typing, and the use of folic acid to prevent spina bifida. It has also supported advancements in diagnosing retinopathy in premature infants. For older children, the charity has funded research into dietary management for liver disease and treatments for burns. Other areas of focus include epilepsy treatment, hip replacement surgery, and the creation of assistive devices for the elderly and severely disabled. These include communication aids, the adaptable matrix wheelchair, and the Tools for Living program. Additionally, the charity has supported research into conditions such as osteoporosis, nerve repair, hydrocephalus, and myasthenia gravis. Currently, the charity is running a campaign called Touching Tiny Lives, which aims to fund research to prevent premature births, pre-eclampsia, and other life-threatening pregnancy complications. The campaign also seeks to improve treatments for babies requiring specialized care. By June 2007, the campaign had raised £2.5 million, with support from celebrities such as Tony Hadley and Martin Fry. The charity is also actively lobbying the UK government to increase funding for research in these areas. This advocacy has resulted in an early day motion introduced by MP Stewart Jackson, which was signed by 69 Members of Parliament. Action Medical Research organizes various fundraising activities. Since 1982, it has held an annual 100-mile sponsored cycling event, which saw 500 participants in 2007. The charity also hosts an annual London-to-Paris sponsored cycle ride, timed to coincide with the Tour de France, as well as numerous local sports events. Another notable event is the annual Bring Your Bear celebration, held on June 25 to mark Paddington Bear's birthday. In 2007, over 500 schools and children's groups participated in this event, which is supported by television personality Zoë Ball. The charity also publishes a magazine for its supporters called Touching Lives, with issues dating back to 2002 available online.
